packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 10 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of these
fragments before reading. I have not tried to identify the work.

====================================================================
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)
====================================================================
What the images show (observation): not a leaf but several narrow parchment strips
reused as spine linings / sewing guards inside the binding of a printed book (a
woodcut printer's device with capital lettering is visible on the facing paper
page; I did not use it). The strips sit between the raised sewing supports.

Images:
- image-001: oblique overview of the gutter, three strip-pieces visible between
  sewing supports (upper, middle, lower); image-002, -003, -004 are oblique
  native-resolution tiles of the same view (upper, middle, lower).
- image-005: flat overview with colour chart and ruler, showing the three exposed
  stubs of the strips; image-006, -007, -008 are flat native-resolution tiles of
  the upper, middle and lower stubs.
- image-009: one piece detached or folded out, seen flat, with the end-band /
  sewing threads lying over its upper middle; image-010 (left half) and image-011
  (right half) are native-resolution tiles of it. The right-hand end of this piece
  is the same parchment as the lower stub in image-008 (same words: "moloch",
  "cor meu(m)", "restaurat..."), where it appears upside down.
- image-012 and image-013: a small, blurred, strongly foreshortened view taken
  inside the spine hollow of a further patch of writing. The two files look
  identical to me.

Script and features (observation): very small, heavily abbreviated book hand in
brown ink, about 2.5-3 mm per line. Many words or short phrases are UNDERLINED in
the same brown ink, and each underlined phrase is followed by ". i ." or ". s ."
and plain text. No rubrics, no coloured initials, no running title visible. No
interlinear gloss; a few suprascript abbreviation letters only.
Tentative interpretation: a continuous commentary in which underlined words are
the lemmata of the text being expounded and the plain text is the exposition.
I keep the two apart below by writing underlined text as _underlined_.

Orientation: upper and middle stubs (image-006, -007) are upright. The lower stub
(image-008) is upside down relative to them. The middle stub has a blank margin
to the LEFT of the writing, so image-007 shows line beginnings; image-006 seems
to show the middle of lines (cut both sides); image-009 shows a piece about
70 mm wide with line beginnings at the left (a blank margin is visible at far
left) and cut at the right.
Columns: cannot be determined from strips this narrow. No complete line survives.

Areas selected: I attempted every exposed line in the flat tiles (006, 007, 008,
010, 011) and used the oblique tiles (002-004) only for the parts hidden in the
gutter. Unread: the text under the sewing threads in the upper middle of
image-009; the inner (gutter) continuation of the upper strip in image-002, which
is out of focus; most of image-012/013.

Conventions: (..) = my expansion; word(?) = uncertain; [illegible] = unreadable;
[ at the end or start of a line = text cut by the edge of the strip;
(et) = tironian sign; _.._ = underlined on the parchment.
Because of the size of the script and the degree of abbreviation, MOST readings
below are uncertain even where not individually marked.

====================================================================
2. UPPER STUB - image-006 (upright; both line ends cut)
====================================================================
image-006 L1   [tops cut] ]p[..]  [..] sec(?)[
image-006 L2   ]_[..]ord(?) ce[..]_ q(u)a(?) ma[             [suprascript a over q]
image-006 L3   ]seq(ui)t(ur)(?) iux(ta)(?) exore(?)[         [a horizontal rule under this line]
image-006 L4   ]lt . (con)posuit sal(?)[
image-006 L5   ]ivitate(?) plenas(?)[                        [perhaps "[c]ivitate"]
image-006 L6   ]bu(m) dd (with stroke) no(n) e(st) all[
image-006 L7   ]_xore(m)(?) mea(m)_ i(n) v(er)ba d[
image-006 L8   ]_udicete(?) p(ro)p(ter)(?)_ . id(e)o(?) p[
image-006 L9   ]lla die saleb(?)[..]t(?)[                    [third word could be "soleb.." or "sedeb.."]
image-006 L10  ]_uda_ (et)c(etera) . h(ic) i(n)sinu[
image-006 L11  ]q(uod)(?) loco (et) domo d[
image-006 L12  ]q(ua)m li[ ... ]ag[                          [middle covered by a paper flap]
image-006 L13  ]e[..][                                       [tops only]

The same stub is seen obliquely in image-002 (L1-L11 there = L2-L12 here; overlap,
no new text). To the right of it in image-002 a further band of writing recedes
into the gutter; it is out of focus and I could not read connected words.

====================================================================
3. MIDDLE STUB - image-007 (upright; line BEGINNINGS, right side cut)
====================================================================
image-007 L1   [a cross-like mark, with two small suprascript letters "u i"(?) to its right]
image-007 L2   _i(n)dig(?)[..]ac(?)_[                        [perhaps "i(n)dig(n)ac.."]
image-007 L3   psaltu(m)(?) . [                              [or "paultu(m)"]
image-007 L4   cultu(m) un[
image-007 L5   dictu(m) i[
image-007 L6   _(et) b(e)n(e)fic_[
image-007 L7   q(uod)(?) s(?) p(ro)p(?) c[                   [several suprascript letters; unresolved]
image-007 L8   _(et) tam(?)[..]_[                            [perhaps "(et) tame(n)"]
image-007 L9   eg(?) (et)c(etera) . i . [
image-007 L10  glo(sa)(?) . cassi[                           [abbreviated "glo." followed by "cassi" and the cut]
image-007 L11  d(omi)no i(n) sp(irit)u[
image-007 L12  _ap(osto)lo(?) o(mn)e(?)_[
image-007 L13  de l(?) p(?)o with "am" written above [
image-007 L14  _(et) psal(?)[..]bo_[                         [perhaps "psallabo"; cf. image-011 L9]

Gutter continuation of these same lines, from the oblique tile image-003. The
lines curve into the fold; pairing with image-007 line numbers is approximate, so
I number them on image-003 itself (counting only the lines of the continuation
band, from the top of the band, right of the stub):

image-003 band L1   ]illibat(?)[..] . (et) [illegible][
image-003 band L2   ][..]aup(er)(?) . (et) daba(?)[t] eis(?)[
image-003 band L3   ]ut p(?) . s . q(?) mi[
image-003 band L4   ]me . un[..]s(?) dic[
image-003 band L5   ](et) terra(m)(?) . ecce me q(?)[..] fue[
image-003 band L6   ]d(?) [..]na(m)(?) ad b(e)n(e)fac[
image-003 band L7   ]. i . ut mala d[
image-003 band L8   ][..] lue(?) . dd (with stroke) . gaudiu(m) m[
image-003 band L9   ](con)fes(?)[..] . manifeste p(ro)dit(?) in[
image-003 band L10  ]ege(?) . iii . abiciit(?) me[
image-003 band L11  ]ut in ea(?) h(?)[..] nata(?)[
image-003 band L12  ]natural(?)[..] . s(ed)(?) d(?) i(n) me[
image-003 band L13  ][illegible] tond(?)[
These thirteen lines are low-confidence readings from an oblique, partly
unfocused view.

====================================================================
4. DETACHED / FOLDED-OUT PIECE - image-009 (tiles image-010 left, image-011 right)
====================================================================
Line numbers are counted on image-009 from the top line of writing; the same
lines appear in image-010 (left ends) and image-011 (right ends), which overlap
in the middle. The piece is in two layers at the left (a narrower left-hand slip
with line beginnings overlaps the main piece), so the left-hand slip and the main
piece may not be the same lines; I give them separately.

4a. Left-hand slip (image-010, far left; line beginnings; right ends hidden)
image-010 L1   ut(?)[
image-010 L2   p(er)(?) mala(?)[                             [or "p(er)mol.."]
image-010 L3   hui(us)(?) s(ed)(?) da[
image-010 L4   vias(?) . q(?) m[
image-010 L5   ii . ut[
image-010 L6   q(uo)d o(?)[..][
image-010 L7   _P(ro)videb_[
image-010 L8   ab hos[
image-010 L9   _no(n) p(ro)pt_[
image-010 L10  d(ici)t d(omi)n(u)s(?) a[
image-010 L11  eni(m)(?) a[
image-010 L12  P(?)adi[                                      [or "p(er)adi.."]

4b. Main piece, right-hand part (image-011; also image-008 upside down)
image-011 L1   ][..]ue p(?)o uta(?)[..][                     [top line, partly cut]
image-011 L2   ]_[..]ut inve(n)iet(?)_ . i . d(?)[..]olat(?)[
image-011 L3   ]p(er)erat(?) ydolu(m) amonitar(um)(?)[
image-011 L4   ][..] suo moloch morte(m)(?)[
image-011 L5   ]_[..]i cor meu(m)_ . i . no(n) app[
image-011 L6   ][..] honorabile . _Et ne_ . h(ic) po(n)it(?)[
image-011 L7   ]so(?) amissor(um)(?) (et)(?) restaurat(i)o(n)em(?) . _et_[
image-011 L8   ]. agn(?) . Jnsup(er)(?) p(?)o q(?)t i(n)clinac(?)[
image-011 L9   ](et) duct(?)[..]ni(?) . _psallabo(?)_ . e[   [suprascript "te"(?) above the underlined word]
image-011 L10  ]d(?) . ut(?) s(cilicet) (con)struer(e)(?) . _(et) ne_[
image-011 L11  ](et)c(etera) . p(ro)p(ter) ista . s(cilicet) mal[
image-011 L12  ]_ad q(ua)s(?) vera(?) (con)sumi(?)_[          [whole line underlined; see 4c L12]

Overlap note: image-008 shows image-011 L2-L12 again, inverted; not new text. In
image-008 the words "ydolu(m) amonitar(um)(?)", "suo moloch", "cor meu(m) . i .
no(n) app", "(h)onorabile . Et ne . h(ic) po(n)it(?)", "restaurat(i)o(n)em . et",
"p(ro)p(ter) ista . s . mal" are a little clearer than in image-011.

4c. Main piece, middle part (between the left slip and the right part; image-009
centre, image-010 right half, image-011 left third). Upper five or six lines lie
under the sewing threads and are unread.
image-009 L6   ][illegible] p(ro)mitte(n)s(?) [illegible][
image-009 L7   ](et) q(?) duc(?)[..]t iustor(um)(?) sive [illegible] . agn(?) .   [runs on into image-011 L8]
image-009 L8   ]sec[..]tate(?) . s(?)[..]a sec[..]tat(?)[..] Ad d[..]b(?)[..] |   [a vertical stroke before the right part]
image-009 L9   ][..] . s(ed)(?) ista mala secu(n)t(ur)(?) _R(espon)d(e)t(?) dd (with stroke) d(?)[..]_   [runs on into image-011 L10]
image-009 L10  ][illegible] q(?) ut(?) dece(?)[..] q(?) tal(?)[..] i(n) mari(?) (et)c(etera) .   [runs on into image-011 L11]
image-009 L11  ]_[..]scor(?) e(st) op(er)atio(?) cor(?)[..] s(?) [..]undelis(?) th(?)[..]_   [underlined; runs on into image-011 L12]
image-009 L12  ]a manu(m)(?) cu(m)(?) d[illegible] m[illegible][   [bottom line, lower halves cut]
A whitish deposit (adhesive/cobweb-like residue) covers the centre of this piece.

====================================================================
5. PATCH INSIDE THE SPINE HOLLOW - image-012 (= image-013, apparently the same photograph)
====================================================================
Strongly foreshortened and blurred; a darker ink and seemingly a slightly larger
script than the stubs, though that may be the lens. Line beginnings at left.
image-012 L1   ascend(?)[..] p(ro)p(ter)(?) fru(?)[
image-012 L2   ccc(?) . xi(?) . [illegible]                  [a small "i" below the first letters]
image-012 L3   _surge(?)_ p(ro)p(ter)(?) multa(?) [
image-012 L4   Et sic(?) [illegible] b(?)n(?)s(?)[
image-012 L5   q(?) d(omi)no (con)iu(n)g(?)[..][
image-012 L6   [..]ulis a(n)i(m)e(?) au[
image-012 L7   q(uod)(?) i(n) magn(?)[
image-012 L8   i(n)icha(?)[..] . se(?) q(?)[
image-012 L9   p(ro)(?) d(omi)no ab(?)[
image-012 L10-L13  [illegible - out of focus]

====================================================================
6. DELETIONS, ADDITIONS, LIMITATIONS
====================================================================
- No deletions or marginal additions seen. The underlinings look original to the
  text (same ink).
- Every line is incomplete; no line can be followed from beginning to end, and
  the order of the strips relative to one another is unknown. I have not joined
  strips into continuous text, apart from noting that image-011 continues the
  lines of image-009's middle part and that image-008 is the same piece inverted.
- I cannot tell whether the upper stub, the middle stub and the detached piece
  come from one leaf. The hand and the underlining practice look alike.
- The double-d abbreviation with a stroke occurs several times (image-006 L6,
  image-003 band L8, image-009 L9); I have left it unexpanded.
- Section 3's gutter continuation and section 5 are the weakest readings.
- To improve this: flat, in-focus, raking-light images of each strip after
  lifting (both sides), especially the middle strip's gutter half and the
  detached piece without the threads lying over it; and a sharp image of the
  patch in image-012.

This is an unverified image reading.

Reader activity: opened PROMPT.md and
image-001.jpg through image-013.jpg (all thirteen).
In addition, because the lower stub is upside down, I made 180-degree rotated
working copies of image-008.jpg and image-004.jpg in my session scratchpad with
the system image tool and viewed one of them (a rotated crop of image-008);
these are derived only from the packet images and contain nothing else.
I did not open packet.json or any other file.
